content.overview: Salient features of administrative tribunals typically include statutory creation, specialised jurisdiction, flexible procedure, mixed legal and technical membership, and limited but real finality subject to judicial review.
content.glance: List the defining features of the tribunal in issue; contrast with ordinary courts; identify which features support constitutionality and which raise concern.
content.study: Tribunals are creatures of statute. Their jurisdiction is defined by the parent Act. Procedure is often less formal than the Code of Civil Procedure, with power to regulate their own procedure subject to statute. Membership may combine judicial and expert members. Decisions may be final on facts subject to statutory appeal and constitutional judicial review. Independence of the adjudicatory process is a critical feature. Current-law framing: ground the analysis in the parent statute and Constitution. Do not treat BSA 2023 as the source of this doctrine.

sections.heading: Specialised Jurisdiction
sections.body: Subject-matter confined to the parent statute.

sections.heading: Procedure
sections.body: Flexibility within statutory and fairness constraints.

sections.heading: Composition
sections.body: Judicial and technical members as provided by law.

sections.heading: Finality and Review
sections.body: Statutory finality does not exclude constitutional judicial review.

examples.title: Specialised jurisdiction
examples.body: A tribunal decides only disputes within its parent statute. That specialisation is a defining feature, not a defect.

examples.title: Finality clause
examples.body: A statute says tribunal decisions are final. Constitutional High Court review under Articles 226/227 still remains.

hypotheticals.question: Does flexible procedure mean natural justice does not apply?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Fairness still constrains tribunal procedure.

hypotheticals.question: Do expert members make legal principles irrelevant?
hypotheticals.analysis: Law and fairness still govern; expertise aids fact-finding.

distinctions.title: Tribunal features vs court features
distinctions.right: Constitutional general jurisdiction and formal procedure

misconceptions.trap: Flexible procedure means natural justice does not apply.
Expert members make legal principles irrelevant.
misconceptions.correction: Law and fairness still govern; expertise aids fact-finding.

cases.name: L. Chandra Kumar v Union of India
cases.issue: What are the defining constitutional features of tribunal adjudication?
cases.ratioDecidendi: Tribunals are specialised adjudicatory bodies whose decisions remain subject to High Court judicial review.
cases.holding: Tribunal model affirmed subject to constitutional supervision.

cases.name: Union of India v Madras Bar Association
cases.issue: What institutional features are constitutionally necessary?
cases.ratioDecidendi: Independence, impartiality, proper qualifications and secure conditions are central to valid tribunal design.
cases.holding: Defective aspects of the framework invalidated.

cases.name: Rojer Mathew v South Indian Bank Ltd.
cases.issue: What constitutional constraints govern tribunal administration?
cases.ratioDecidendi: Executive control over adjudicatory institutions is constrained by independence requirements.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a tribunals-features problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. List statutory features. II. Test fairness and independence. III. Identify review pathway. IV. Conclude.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What should submissions contain?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Features identified; independence analysis; review route; precise relief.

examTips: Note review residual under L. Chandra Kumar.

enhancement.definition: Tribunals are statutory specialised adjudicatory bodies with flexible procedure and residual constitutional review.
enhancement.legalPrinciple: Features follow from the parent statute; flexibility is not lawlessness; finality clauses cannot bar constitutional review.
enhancement.detailedExplanation: Tribunals are creatures of statute with specialised jurisdiction.
enhancement.problemApplication: List features; test independence; identify review.
keyTakeaways: Features follow from the parent statute.
Finality clauses cannot bar constitutional review.
